text:
alin: heads up — we saw 3x p95 tail on eu-west-dedicated pool this morning, looked like a locality hotspot. can someone sanity-check placement + failover config?

maria: saw alerts. p50 fine, p95 jumped from 220ms -> 1.1s around 06:12 UTC, correlated with a single rack network flapping. noisy neighbor? possibly a heavy embedding job.

sam: is this affecting only dedicated slices or shared too?

alin: only dedicated slices pinned to az-3, shared traffic routed across az-1/2 unaffected.

leo: quick data: slice-util shows one tenant spiking GPU mem+PCIe utilization, nvlink errors in kernel logs. suspect that colocated batch job congested PCIe fabric causing preemptive context switches.

jia: can we fast-failover slices to warmpool in a different AZ? current routing policy has a 30s cooldown + cross-az penalty. that penalty is too high for this severity.

maria: agree — lowering cross-az penalty to allow immediate fallback for p95 > 800ms would help availability but raises cost. what's the tolerance?

alin: for SLO-critical tenants we should enable immediate cross-az fallback. propose a new policy: 
```
policy: {
  trigger: p95_latency > 800ms for 2m,
  action: failover_to_warmpool(zone_select=least_loaded, allow_cross_az=true, max_cost_multiplier=1.3)
}
```

sam: also, we need a hard cap on batch jobs on dedicated nodes — they should be throttled by queue size, not allowed to saturate PCIe. can we add a nic-police and pci-shed ejection?

leo: yes. suggested ejection rule: if nvlink_errors > 5/min or pcie_util > 85% for 1m -> evict non-critical pods with backoff.

jia: operational playbook notes?

maria: quick playbook draft in thread:
- detect: p95 latency > 800ms && nvlink_errors > 3/min
- mitigate: lower cross-az penalty, trigger warmpool failover, bump dedicated burst capacity by 1 slice for 5m
- isolate: mark host in quarantine label 'pcie-flap' and drain non-essentials
- postmortem: collect nvlink/kernel logs, dmesg, nvidia-smi sample, and slice allocation logs

alin: can someone run the verification query against telemetry? i want a list of affected slice ids last 24h and which tenants triggered warmpool fallback in past 7d.

sam: running now: `curl -s "http://telemetry.internal/api/v1/query?m=dedicated_slice_events&since=24h" | jq .`

devops-bot: deploy-check: placement-policy v2.4.1 applied to eu-west yesterday 03:45 UTC by @deploy-bot :white_check_mark:

leo: results: 7 slices had p95 breaches, 4 triggered fallback. two of those were manual canaries for a large infra test. remaining 3 belong to tenant 'vector-embeddings' — they had long-running batch training starting 02:00 UTC.

jia: vector-embeddings should be in soft-isolation profile. why were they allowed on pinned dedicated?

maria: their reservation was created as dedicated through onboarding script last quarter. mislabeling. we should auto-validate tenant workload shape vs pool type at commit time.

alin: action items:
- sam: add pci-e error based ejection rule + throttle for batch jobs (ETA 2d)
- jia: lower cross-az penalty for p95-triggered failover, add per-tenant opt-in flag for cross-az auto-failover for SLO-critical (ETA 1d)
- leo: build query for 7d warmpool fallbacks and tag misclassified tenants (ETA today)
- maria: add validation check in onboarding pipeline to reject dedicated pins for heavy batch profiles (ETA 3d)

sam: i'll open PR for ejection rule. tiny config preview: 
```yaml
eviction:
  nvlink_error_threshold: 5
  pcie_util_threshold: 85
  window: 60s
  target: non_critical_pods
  backoff: 5m
```

jia: cross-az penalty change: lowering from 0.8 -> 0.2 for p95-triggered only. will patch routing engine and run canary for eu-west-staging first.

devops-bot: canary rollout started: routing-engine v1.9.4 -> staging-eu-west at 2026-03-20T08:23:00Z

maria: one more note — billing estimation if cross-az failover triggers often: we should surface cost delta per-tenant in console so product can reach out. otherwise finance will get surprised.

alin: good point. add cost delta telemetry for warmpool cross-az events.

sam: ok i'll include cost tags in the fallback event payload.

leo: for short-term mitigation i manually evicted the two noisy pods on host rack-az3-12 and rebalanced their slices to warmpool; p95 back to ~240ms. monitor for 30m.

jia: monitoring: added temporary alert rule with higher sensitivity on nvlink errors and p95 spikes. if it fires more than twice in 1h escalate to oncall.

maria: thanks team. please update the tickets with links to PRs and telemetry queries. :thumbsup:

alin: leaving notes in infra-runbook and will schedule a post-incident review tomorrow.

sam: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/821

leo: keeping an eye. will post logs if next spike happens.

devops-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-0320-17 — assigned to eng-infra oncall.
